connection: Session 03 classified a variance inline. This session extracts that work into named methods and makes data flow and scope explicit.
objectives: Identify a method signature, arguments, parameters, and return value.
Trace values into and out of a method call.
Extract repeated or conceptually named work without changing behavior.

visuals.title: Arguments enter a method
visuals.explanation: A call supplies argument values to parameters; control enters the method and later returns to the caller.

visuals.title: Parameters and locals stay scoped
visuals.explanation: Parameters and local variables are available inside their method boundary, preventing unrelated code from depending on temporary details.

visuals.title: Return sends one result back
visuals.explanation: A return value crosses the method boundary and lets the caller decide what to do with the result.

visuals.title: The signature is a contract
visuals.explanation: Return type, method name, and parameter list describe how callers may use the method.

preQuiz.prompt: What is scheduledHours in CalculateVariance(entry, scheduledHours)?
options: An argument at the call site
preQuiz.explanation: The call supplies the current value as an argument; the method receives it through a parameter.

preQuiz.prompt: Can a local variable declared inside CalculateVariance be read directly in top-level code?
options: No, its scope is the method body
preQuiz.explanation: A local is only in scope within its declaring block.

preQuiz.prompt: Why return a decimal from CalculateVariance?
options: So the caller receives the calculated value
preQuiz.explanation: The method produces a decimal result that the caller can store or use.

concept.title: A method names a unit of behavior
paragraphs: A method groups statements behind a name. A good name lets the caller express intent while the body owns calculation details.
Extraction is useful when it clarifies responsibility, not merely to make code shorter.

concept.title: Parameters receive values
paragraphs: Arguments are expressions at the call site. Parameters are local names in the method declaration. By default, C# passes the resulting values by value.
The ClockEntry argument value is a reference, so the method and caller can refer to the same object; deeper reference behavior is taught later.
concept.code: static decimal CalculateVariance(ClockEntry entry, decimal scheduledHours)

concept.title: Scope limits dependencies
paragraphs: recordedHours exists only inside CalculateVariance. scheduleStatus exists only inside ClassifyVariance. Those boundaries prevent temporary details from leaking into unrelated statements.
return ends the method and supplies its result to the caller.

lab.objective: Extract variance calculation and classification into local methods without changing output.
lab.startingCondition: Program.cs calculates recordedHours, varianceHours, and scheduleStatus inline.
steps: Predict which variables will no longer be visible in top-level code.
Create CalculateVariance with ClockEntry and decimal parameters and a decimal return type.
Move recorded-hours conversion and subtraction into CalculateVariance.
Create ClassifyVariance with a decimal parameter and string return type.
Replace inline work with method calls, then build, run, and test.
lab.expectedBehavior: Console output remains +0.50 hours and over schedule; all tests pass.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet run --project src/TimeClock.App/TimeClock.App.csproj --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

expectedFiles.why: Extract named methods and demonstrate parameters, returns, and scope.

commit: session-04: teach methods parameters scope and returns
review: Method names describe results rather than mechanics.
Parameter and return types match the values crossing each boundary.
Temporary variables have the narrowest useful scope.
Build and tests pass without warnings.

postQuiz.prompt: Where is recordedHours available after extraction?
postQuiz.explanation: It is a local declared in that method body.

postQuiz.prompt: What changes if CalculateVariance returns scheduledHours - recordedHours?
options: The sign and meaning of variance
postQuiz.explanation: Reversing operands preserves compilation but changes semantics.

postQuiz.prompt: Why can ClassifyVariance be tested through application output here?
postQuiz.explanation: The caller displays the returned status, making the result observable.

reflections: Which details became hidden after extraction?
When would a method with many parameters signal a design problem?
How does return type constrain callers?
whatBreaks: Removing CalculateVariance leaves the caller without the numeric result. Removing a return statement prevents a non-void method from compiling. Moving recordedHours outside the method widens scope and weakens the boundary even if behavior remains the same.
summary: Methods name behavior. Arguments produce values for parameters, locals stay within scope, and return values carry results back to callers.
